prs.title: fix(client): release SSE reader locks
prs.author: Genmin
prs.reason: [llm] cluster primary: SSE reader lock in StreamableHTTPClientTransport is never released when the read loop exits, pinning the underlying reader-tied buffer in memory (~50MB per long-lived client) until GC. Both PRs patch the exact same location in src/client/streamableHttp.ts (right after `.getReader()`), replacing the bare `while (true) { const { value: event, done } = await reader.read(); ... }` loop with the identical loop wrapped in a `try` block so the reader lock can be released afterward — the removed/added lines shown in both diffs are structurally identical. (2 PRs)
prs.short_reason: [llm] cluster primary: SSE reader lock in StreamableHTTPClientTransport is never released when the read loop exits, pinning the underlying reader-tied buffer in memory (~50MB per long-lived client) until GC. prs.cluster_pick_reason: Both PRs make the identical code change (same try-wrap around the same reader loop at the same line, same file, same base revision). The differentiator is the scope each author states in their .changeset: #1998 says it releases the lock 'after graceful closes or read errors,' i.e. covers both the normal-completion exit and the error/exception exit path, while #1961's changeset only describes releasing the lock 'on disconnect' and doesn't mention the read-error path. A fix that only wraps the success path but not a catch for read errors leaves the leak reachable whenever `reader.read()` throws, so #1998's broader stated coverage is the more complete fix to keep.
